newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar off highs as dlr/majors recover.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar off highs as dlr/majors recover.

text.p: The Singapore dollar remained firm but was off its morning highs in late Asian trade as the U.S. dollar made a partial recovery against the major currencies, dealers said.
The domestic unit was quoted at 1.4340/50 to the U.S. dollar at 0830 GMT against its opening 1.4380/85.
It earlier rose to a near two-month high around 1.4300/05 in line with the U.S. dollar's steep drop to a four-month low of 117.50 yen. The dollar was at 118.51/61 yen at 0830 GMT.
"Basically the dollar/majors just recovered some of their losses," a European bank dealer said, adding that this had helped lift the dollar/Sing.
She said the U.S. dollar was likely to trade a 1.4330-1.4380 range against the Singapore dollar, with the 1.4400 level expected to pose stiff resistance for the next week at least.

Dealers said active buying of the U.S. dollar by local banks around its morning low spurred speculation of intervention by the de facto central bank, pushing the U.S. dollar back above the 1.4300 area.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore typically intervenes in forex markets through major local banks to stem any sharp moves in the Singapore dollar. It does not comment on its interventions.
"The local banks were buying dollars around the 1.4300/05. That's why it bounced up so fast to 1.4330/35," a European bank dealer said.
She said the U.S. unit should be supported around 1.4300 for the time being and players were likely to sell into any rallies towards the 1.4350 level.
"The market's still very long the dollar/Sing and ringgit/Sing cross so a lot of stop-losses were triggered," a U.S. bank dealer said.
